label: WeftFS-Go KV prefix parity: tier, scope checks, Ed25519 verification, bidirectional handoff, per-page cost

rust_oracle.path: weftfs (built with `cargo build --release --bin weftfs`, no fuse feature)
rust_oracle.note: the fuse build needs libfuse3, absent from the go court; the oracle is the non-fuse binary

ed25519.mechanism: Store.KvPrefixGetVerified loads the stored signed envelope blob and verifies it with WeftCodec-Go capability.Verify (Go standard library crypto/ed25519), then builds the scope with auth.NewCapability.
ed25519.trusted_verifier_boundary_retained: Store.KvPrefixGet still accepts an already-verified *auth.Capability; that is the historical Go boundary and is labelled as such in the source.
ed25519.cross_language: a Go-signed grant is verified by Rust (kv get --envelope) and a Rust-written prefix is read by Go with a Go-verified grant

cost.label: Go per-page cost: batched publication and scoped reads; one host

mutual_exclusion.identical_record_bytes: Go ParseKvPrefixRecord round-trips Rust records and recomputes the same canonical bytes and id; the cross test reads a Rust-written record and a Go-written record is read by Rust
mutual_exclusion.identical_lookup_verdicts: Go reproduces the exact compatibility rule; the same token sequence matches and a one-token drift does not

non_claims: no Go index (T063 persisted index is Rust-only); Go lookup is the oracle scan
no Go mode-19 or mode-15 writer
one host, synthetic pages, warm cache; no fleet/cloud claim
the per-page cost is a single-process measurement, not a service SLO
